readings.span: **It means “we’ll discuss this later” (or “not now”), often as a polite delay or deferral.**
Combined with walking away mid-conversation, it usually signals the manager is ending the discussion for now rather than addressing the raise immediately.
They need time to review performance data, company policy, budget, or talk to HR/finance.
The timing or setting wasn’t right (hallway/impromptu chat instead of a scheduled meeting).
They’re postponing a potentially uncomfortable conversation.
Less positively, it can be a soft brush-off if they don’t want to commit or hope the topic fades.
It’s not an automatic “no,” but it’s also not a commitment.

valence.span: The lines describe a simple, vivid rural scene and assert that "so much depends" on these ordinary objects.
valence.label: neutral

readings.span: Everyday objects and scenes matter more than we usually notice; the wheelbarrow (useful farm tool), rain (necessary for growth), and chickens form an interdependent, ordinary world that "so much depends upon."
It celebrates direct perception and the power of a clear image—the "glazed" wetness and color contrast make the scene vivid and self-sufficient.
Some interpretations treat it as a comment on rural/farm life, labor, or simply the act of seeing itself.
